newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - PepsiCo trades lower.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - PepsiCo trades lower.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc's share price fell preceding Friday's U.S. market open, surrendering gains that came in after-hours trade last night on news of a restructuring overseas and related charges.
The gains late Thursday came in thin trade and were wiped out early Friday as investors "had all evening to digest" the news, a trader said.
Ahead of the opening bell, PepsiCo fell to 29-7/8 after trading as high as 31-3/4 last night.
The shares ended yesterday's regular New York Stock Exchange session at 30-1/4.
After the market close Thursday, the food and beverage giant said it expects third quarter earnings per share to be about $0.30 below the $0.77 posted a year earlier.
The decline was attributed to an estimated $360 million, or $0.21 per share, pre-tax charge incurred in a restructuring of its international beverage business, among other moves.
Investor apprehension about the news was confirmed when PepsiCo announced early Friday that 1997 earnings were expected to be $0.10 below analysts' forecasts.
The stock continued lower in later pre-open trade, hitting 29-3/8.
General Electric Co is expected to rise to at least 91 from 90-3/8 when the market opens, traders said.
Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to its recommended list from market outperformer, according to a market source.
There was no activity in the shares of A.H. Belo Corp or Providence Journal Co because trading remained halted for news dissemination.
Last night Belo announced the acquisition of Providence for $1.5 billion in cash and stock, forming one of the largest U.S. media companies.
Belo shares closed at 37-1/2, and Providence at 20-3/4.
ValuJet Inc said it plans to resume flights on Monday. Its shares rose to 13-1/2 from 12-7/8 before the open.
Traders said they expect Mackie Designs to fall sharply when trade commences. They cited the company's warning that third quarter earnings are expected to be below analysts' estimates.
The shares were bid at seven, asked at 7-1/2, after closing Thursday in Nasdaq trade at 9-1/2.
